content.thinking:
I'm piecing together the postmortem narrative, starting with the symptom that account pages failed for shoppers, then tracing the causal chain through the citations and error rate metrics that spiked during the incident.

Next, I identify the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 as the proximate cause, then trace it back to the monthly-spend-feature flag being enabled, which routed evaluations down the new code path. I'm ruling out alternative causes — deployments and ongoing rollouts — by checking that there was only one production change that day (the flag itself) and that replicas had converged on a single revision.

The root cause: the new monthly spend summary logic divides the shopper's month total by the count of this-month purchases, and for shoppers with past purchases but none in the current month, that count is zero, triggering the division error. This checks out against a single confirmed reading of the function's logic, with no further mechanism needed to explain the failure.

Turning monthly-spend-feature back on without fixing the code would likely reproduce the same failure for shoppers with no purchases this month, since the flag was switched off but the underlying bug was never patched.

CF-1: The flag rolled out to most traffic at once with no gradual ramp or guardrail, so a staged rollout with automatic halt on error spikes would have limited the blast radius.

CF-2: No existing test covered the no-purchases path for the monthly summary, which the proposed fix should address alongside the code patch. I'm also noting that nobody appears to have been paged when the errors began.

Given that Argus resolved the issue within minutes on its own, paging likely wouldn't have shortened the incident, so I'll leave this as a mild went_wrong note — the alert never reached an on-call person even though no human intervention was actually needed here.

For CF-4, I'm folding the admin toggle issue into CF-1 as part of the gradual rollout gap, keeping CF-2 focused on test coverage. For action items, I'm proposing progressive flag rollout to avoid flipping something on for all traffic simultaneously, and considering whether to add automatic flag rollback on error spikes, though Argus already effectively did that.

I'm noting what went well: Argus traced the issue to the flag change and switched it off shortly after the alert fired, then confirmed the service returned to normal levels after the alert was raised.

Code-Fix proposed a draft PR #363 after the alert was raised. What went wrong was that the admin's flag switch enabled the path for most traffic at once, and no one paged. As for luck, the fault only affected shoppers with no purchases this month, and the flag being instantly revertible wasn't chance, so I'll leave that empty. For assumptions, the empty this-month purchase list mechanism comes from Code-Fix's static reading, customer loss is measured against prior weeks, and the ClientDisconnected errors before onset should be treated as part of the baseline.

I'm also assuming the revision read at T10 matched the pre-onset state since no deploy came back. I won't mention detection timing in the lessons section. For the first step, I'm citing the account page error rate spike to 36 at 16:31. Now I'm drafting the timing for when the admin switched on the monthly-spend-feature flag and cross-referencing when flag evaluations resumed versus when pages rendered normally beforehand, working through which metric label corresponds to the "on" state.

The disabling of the flag at T18/T21 confirms the fix, so I'll cite T21 as the confirming evidence. I've ruled out a deploy as the cause since T8/T9 show the only production change that day was the flag flip, and T15 confirms it's the only flag change by anyone besides Argus in that hour. That settles it, so I'm ready to write the final summary.

action_items.item: Switch flags such as monthly-spend-feature on for a small share of traffic first, and widen it in steps rather than for all traffic at once.
Hold or reverse a flag rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises after the flag changes.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix proposed in PR #363 is in production.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is told when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that failed rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average, with a worst of {errors_at_worst}, and the service's own warnings showed the account page error rate at its highest at {Gbac1.7}.

Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appeared at the onset and was logged {G5309.1} times from {G5309.3}. Before the onset, the only account page error logged was a shopper closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: no deploys came back for the day before the onset, and the flag toggle was the only production change read.
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed only the one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read.
A rollout still in progress: as of {T10.1}, all replicas were running one revision.

causal_chain.step: At {P1.1}, admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature. Before that, every evaluation came back off and account pages rendered normally. In the minute {G971b.6}, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and every evaluation after that came back on. Switching the flag back off brought the service back from the incident's level, and that action was judged confirmed.

Code-Fix read that, with the flag on, the account page's spend summary divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of items bought this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division fails at line {F1.1}, the line the logged error points to.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending summary on account pages, and it likely tried to divide by the number of items the shopper had bought this month, which cannot work for shoppers who have bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag reached almost all account page traffic at once. In the first minute, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and after that every evaluation came back on. No staged rollout, and no automatic hold on a rise in errors, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Turning the flag on for a small share of traffic first would have limited the failures to that share, and the rise in errors could have been caught before it reached most shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the monthly spend summary for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix had to write new cases to cover it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have failed on the division before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: Argus traced the failures to the flag change and switched monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft fix, PR #363, {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so no person was told while the incident ran.

input.root_cause: The account page's monthly spend summary, which runs only when monthly-spend-feature is on, divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of items bought this month (line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py). For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list of items is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The failing code path was left unchanged when the flag was switched off, so turning monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
